brief.headline: Press for 60-day credit extension and qualify Manjushree as second source — Kilitch is a trader in the Altman grey zone with a 2/10 financial score.

priceAsk.summary: Hold price, benchmark to HDPE resin market line
priceAsk.target: Track HDPE resin import unit value at 87.61 ₹/kg
priceAsk.basis: Kilitch is 100.0% trader carrying reseller margin; their price should move with the HDPE resin market line at 87.61 ₹/kg, and we should verify they're not layering excessive margin on traded goods.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Extend our credit from 30 days to 60 or 90 days
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹5.36 L working capital currently tied; extension would free additional capital proportionally

brief.financialLeverage: Kilitch's 2.8% net margin sits just below the peer median of 3.1%, and their -5.1% EBITDA margin signals operational stress. They're in the Altman grey zone (Z=1.58) with a weak Probe42 score of 2/10 and pending legal cases. Our ₹65.27 L annual spend represents 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue — meaningful volume leverage. However, they already stretch payables to 105d versus the peer median of 57d, so they understand extended credit. Given the thin margin and distress signal, we avoid a hard price squeeze that risks supply continuity; instead, we push payment terms (they can afford to wait — receivables are only 48d) and qualify a robust second source to de-risk concentration.

evidence.point: Kilitch is purely a trader, not a manufacturer
Our spend is a significant share of their business
evidence.figure: ₹65.27 L annual spend is 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They already extend payables far beyond peers
Financial health is weak with distress signals
evidence.figure: Probe42 score 2/10, Altman Z 1.58 (grey zone), health score C (55/100)

evidence.point: Margins are razor-thin with negative operating profit
evidence.figure: 2.8% net margin, -5.1% EBITDA margin versus peer median 3.1% net

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue with B health score (65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms capability makes them the top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹946.50 Cr revenue with B health score (73/100) — strong, profitable manufacturer for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging player at ₹701.17 Cr revenue with broad bottle/cap capability across rigid plastics

risks: Altman Z of 1.58 puts Kilitch in the grey zone — risk of financial distress means over-concentration or aggressive price pressure could destabilize a fragile supplier and disrupt our supply
2/10 Probe42 financial score and pending legal cases signal supply-continuity risk — we need a qualified second source before pushing hard on commercial terms
They collect receivables in only 48d while we pay at 30d — extending our payment may face resistance despite their own 105d payables, so frame it as alignment with their industry practice
100.0% traded revenue means they have no manufacturing moat — if we push too hard on price they may simply stop carrying our SKUs or pass through supplier increases with no buffer
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and given you're working on 105-day payables with your own suppliers while our volumes represent 1.19% of your revenue, we'd like to discuss moving to 60- or 90-day terms and ensuring we have a second qualified source for supply security.
